lawRefs: K.S.A. 79-32,110 (rates) as amended by 2024 Special Session SB 1
2025 SB 269 (contingent future rate cuts; none triggered for 2026 per KDOR Notice 25-06)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rates and standard deduction from the 2026 Form K-40ES; exemption and 65+ amounts from the 2025 K-40 instructions (statutory, unchanged for 2026; KDOR's 2026 legislative summary shows no rate, deduction or exemption changes and HB 2629 to raise the standard deduction failed). Two brackets: 5.2% up to $23,000 ($46,000 MFJ), 5.58% above; head of household and MFS use the single schedule. Standard deduction: single $3,605, MFJ $8,240, MFS $4,120, HOH $6,180; additional $850 per condition (65+/blind) if single or HOH, $700 if married. Personal exemption: $9,160 per taxpayer ($18,320 MFJ), plus $2,320 per dependent. Social Security benefits are fully exempt (since tax year 2024). No general pension/IRA exclusion, but KPERS and other Kansas public pensions, federal civil service and military retirement, and Railroad Retirement are fully exempt.
